title: Heavy checks wait on a machine-wide lock instead of flaking under load
notes: Retro 2026-11-26: with several panes running at once, the load average reached 22-50 on 16 cores, and full test suites timed out and failed at random: one new-crm worker ran vitest 4 times; 'all 13 suites that failed pass alone'. Seen in 3 of 5 new-crm sessions and in pragma. Give the worker panes a machine-wide lock (flock on a file under ~/.cache/dashboard, or one the app holds) that full test, build and typecheck runs wait on, wired so a worker in any project uses it without a project change. The work-card and review prompts also tell the worker to rerun only the failed files, never the whole suite, to confirm a failure is load flake.

comments.body: From main: PR #380 (open) changes src/main/skills/work-card-skill.ts to open PRs with pr create; #382 (merged) rewrote the review prompt in src/main/ship/review.ts. Keep your edits to those files small and merge origin/main in if #380 lands first.

R1 fixed 5 findings in 6f4ade23 (a bare vitest on a terminal is watch mode, so it no longer holds every pane; pnpm/npm -w is the workspace flag, not watch; LONGEST_WAIT comment; sleep moved to its own module; ship and skills history lines). R2 fixed 1 low in 31cf0bd4 (vitest --run / --watch=false on a terminal now waits); the final check accepted it. Neither round changed the card's design. NOT ready to merge: after #380 landed, GitHub reports the PR CONFLICTING/dirty against main 97f7ec8c, but a local git merge-tree of origin/main and 31cf0bd4 merges cleanly, so pr wait could not name the files. CI did not run. Next: merge origin/main into the branch and push, which also makes GitHub recompute, then run pr wait 384 again.
